title: 1 Samuel 1
paragraphs: ¹ There was a man from Ramathaim-Zophim in the hill country of Ephraim named Elkanah son of Jeroham, son of Elihu, son of Tohu, son of Zuph, an Ephrathite. ² He had two wives; one was named Hannah and the other Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah had none. ³ Year after year this man would go up from his town to worship and offer sacrifices to the LORD of Hosts at Shiloh, where Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, served as priests. ⁴ Whenever the day came for Elkanah to sacrifice, he would give portions of the meat to his wife Peninnah and to all her sons and daughters. ⁵ But to Hannah he gave a double portion, because he loved her—and yet the LORD had closed her womb.

⁶ Her rival Peninnah would taunt and provoke her constantly because the LORD had kept her from having children. ⁷ This happened year after year. Whenever Hannah went up to the house of the LORD, Peninnah would mock her until she wept and could not eat. ⁸ Her husband Elkanah would say to her, "Hannah, why are you crying? Why won't you eat? Why are you so heartbroken? Am I not better to you than ten sons?" ⁹ Once, after they had eaten and drunk at Shiloh, Hannah got up. Eli the priest was sitting on a chair by the doorpost of the LORD's temple. ¹⁰ Deeply distressed, she prayed to the LORD and wept bitterly.

¹¹ She made a vow, saying, "LORD of Hosts, if you will look on the suffering of your servant and remember me—if you will not forget me but give me a son—then I will dedicate him to the LORD all the days of his life, and no razor will ever touch his head." ¹² As she continued praying before the LORD, Eli was watching her mouth. ¹³ Hannah was praying silently; her lips were moving but her voice was inaudible, so Eli thought she was drunk. ¹⁴ He said to her, "How long are you going to be drunk? Get rid of your wine." ¹⁵ "No, my lord," Hannah replied, "I am a woman in deep anguish. I haven't been drinking wine or beer; I've been pouring out my soul to the LORD.

¹⁶ Don't take your servant for a worthless woman. I've been speaking all this time out of great anguish and grief." ¹⁷ Then Eli answered, "Go in peace, and may the God of Israel grant what you have asked of him." ¹⁸ "May your servant find favor in your eyes," she said. Then she went her way, ate something, and her face was no longer downcast. ¹⁹ Early the next morning they rose, worshiped before the LORD, and returned home to Ramah. Elkanah made love to his wife Hannah, and the LORD remembered her. ²⁰ Before the year was out, Hannah conceived and gave birth to a son. She named him Samuel, saying, "Because I asked the LORD for him."

²¹ When Elkanah and all his household went up to offer the annual sacrifice and to fulfill his vow to the LORD, ²² Hannah did not go. She told her husband, "After the boy is weaned, I'll take him and present him before the LORD, and he will stay there permanently." ²³ Her husband Elkanah said to her, "Do what seems best to you. Stay home until you have weaned him. May the LORD bring his word to pass." So Hannah stayed and nursed her son until she weaned him. ²⁴ After she had weaned him, she took him up to Shiloh, along with a three-year-old bull, an ephah of flour, and a skin of wine. The boy was still young. They brought him to the house of the LORD. ²⁵ Then they slaughtered the bull and brought the boy to Eli.

²⁶ She said, "Excuse me, my lord. As surely as you live, I am the woman who stood here beside you praying to the LORD. ²⁷ I prayed for this child, and the LORD has given me what I asked of him. ²⁸ So now I'm giving him back to the LORD. For as long as he lives, he is given to the LORD." And they worshiped the LORD there.
